{{Short description|Set of composite numbers}}
{{Refimprove|date=December 2015}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Catalan pseudoprime''' is an odd [[composite number]] ''n'' satisfying the congruence

:<math> (-1)^{\frac{n-1}{2}} \cdot C_{\frac{n-1}{2}} \equiv 2 \pmod n,</math>

where ''C<sub>m</sub>'' denotes the ''m''-th [[Catalan number]]. 

The above congruence holds for every odd [[prime number]] ''n'', so any composite ''n'' that satisfies it is [[pseudoprime]].

== Properties ==

The only known Catalan pseudoprimes are: 5907, 1194649, and 12327121 {{OEIS|A163209}} with the latter two being squares of [[Wieferich prime]]s. In general, if ''p'' is a Wieferich prime, then ''p''<sup>2</sup> is a Catalan pseudoprime.
